errors.location: Artemia salina toxicity methods and results
errors.description: The manuscript reports incompatible test concentrations, so the toxicity findings cannot be assigned to a definite exposure dose.
errors.evidence: Methods: acute test solution “(100.0 mg L⁻¹).” Later, the toxicity discussion refers to “100 μg/L,” and the developmental-toxicity results refer to both “100μg/L” and “100 μg/mL HTS_NFG.”

errors.description: The pilot-batch zeta potential is reported with opposite signs. These values cannot both describe the same measurement, and the polarity matters to the stated particle-charge interpretation.
errors.evidence: Text: pilot-scale zeta potential was “31.48mv” and earlier “+31.48 mv”; Fig. 4d label: “Zeta Potential: -31.48 mV.”

errors.description: The UV assay does not establish that HTS retained biological activity after irradiation. It measures whole-formulation UV–visible spectra, morphology, and particle size, but reports no post-irradiation fungal viability, germination, or insecticidal activity measurement; those observations therefore do not support the conclusion that NFG protects HTS efficacy.
errors.evidence: Methods: after UV exposure, “The UV spectra and morphology of the HTS_NFG were observed” and particle size was monitored. Results: unchanged absorbance is used to conclude that “the self-assembly of NFG provides UV protection to HTS” and enhances UV resistance.
